chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, all together, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqeel, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Let those whom your right hands possess, and those among you who have not yet attained puberty, seek permission from you three times: before the Dawn Prayer, and when you put off your clothes at midday, and after the Evening Prayer. These are three times of privacy for you. There is no blame upon you nor upon them after these times, as they circulate among you. And whoever among you has attained puberty, let him not enter upon his mother, nor his sister, nor his daughter, nor anyone else besides that, except by permission. And let him not permit anyone unless he greets, for the greeting is obedience to the Beneficent.

key_terms.الَّذِينَ مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ: Those whom your right hands possess (servants/slaves)

ai.seo_question: What are the three times of day for seeking permission in Islam according to the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elaborates on the Quranic command for 'istidhan' (seeking permission), specifying three 'awrat' (times of privacy) corresponding to natural breaks in daily activity: before Fajr, at midday, and after Isha. It extends the requirement of permission to those who have reached puberty entering upon close female relatives, emphasizing that the greeting 'salam' is not merely social etiquette but an act of 'ta'at al-Rahman' (obedience to the Merciful), a key concept in Shia jurisprudence linking ritual greeting to divine compliance.
